newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung, Chan to meet Chinese leaders in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung, Chan to meet Chinese leaders in Beijing.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa and the territory's top civil servant Anson Chan are to meet Chinese leaders in Beijing together this week for the first time, the government and Tung's office said on Monday.
Tung, who will govern Hong Kong after Britain hands it back to China on July 1, would visit the Chinese capital on Thursday and Friday, a statement from his office said.
Chan, the current Chief Secretary who is to remain in her post after the handover, would visit Beijing between Thursday and Saturday, a government statement said.
Chan, the top ethnic Chinese official in the British colonial administration, would join Tung to meet Chinese leaders together, the statement added.
Tung and Anson have met Chinese leaders in separate visits in the past, but never together.
Chan, who has served the present government for more than three decades, is sometimes seen as a representative of British colonial rule.

She deputises for Governor Chris Patten, sees to the implementation of government policies and is senior member in the governor's Executive Council, or advisory cabinet, the highest policy-making body in the territory.
Last year, Chan consistently topped popularity polls as a candidate for the territory's post-colonial leader.
